$comment: Generated by canon/_tools/build_catalog.py. Machine twin of CATALOG.md. Read useWhen to choose; filter on the closed vocabularies.

templates.name: A long argument on tinted ground, beside its model
templates.useWhen: A position needs three or four hundred words to be made honestly — a methodology, a privacy stance, a point of view — and the model it rests on has to be visible while the case is being read.

templates.name: Framing column beside a grid of instances
templates.useWhen: One principle has to be stated once and then shown through four to six named instances, and the principle deserves more room than any single instance.

templates.name: Numbered method steps across a ground change
templates.useWhen: A method or approach has three or four named stages, each needing a sentence of substance rather than a label, and the deck has to look like it knows the order matters.

templates.name: Four stages, each with its receipts
templates.useWhen: A transformation happened in four stages and each one needs both a screenshot of what was actually built and the two or three things that changed.

templates.name: Five-stage method with substance under each stage
templates.useWhen: A repeatable method has four or five stages and each stage genuinely has activities and deliverables worth naming — the audience needs to see the depth, not just the sequence.

templates.name: Claim held up by five numbers across a rule
templates.useWhen: A claim about the business needs five pieces of quantitative proof, and the claim itself — not any one number — is what the room should leave with.

templates.name: Sorted into nine bands, not scored on a line
templates.useWhen: Fifteen to twenty-five candidates need prioritising and the scoring is a judgement rather than a measurement — the room will argue about which band something belongs in, not about a decimal place.

templates.name: Everything scored on two axes at once
templates.useWhen: Ten to thirty-five candidates have to be prioritised and the conversation is about relative position — what is nearly equal, what is clearly ahead — not about which named box each one falls in.

templates.name: Four disciplines contained in one system
templates.useWhen: Four capabilities have to be shown as living inside a single system rather than merely sitting next to each other, and the claim needs a paragraph or two to land.

templates.name: Half-bleed image beside a connected sequence
templates.useWhen: An assessment or approach has three to five named moves that belong in order, and the subject deserves a full-height image rather than a caption-sized one.

templates.name: Partner wall organised by category
templates.useWhen: A partner or technology roster has to show BREADTH across named categories, and which category a logo sits in matters as much as the logo being there.

templates.name: Partner credentials compared side by side
templates.useWhen: Two or three platform partnerships each need their own proof — depth of certification, scale of delivery, and who it was delivered for — and the point is that all of them are strong.

templates.name: Who is in the room
templates.useWhen: Four to six people are being introduced at the top of a meeting and each needs placing by role and location — not a biography.
